editorial:
Imagine you are back in the old west, where love letters were the only way to tell someone you liked them. You get to follow Jode, a sweet cowboy who is totally head over heels for his boss's daughter, Peg. The problem is that Jode is not exactly a wordsmith, so he gets a buddy to write a romantic letter for him. Things get wild when a Native American man steals the letter and delivers it to Peg himself. It is a lighthearted ride with a lot of heart, focusing on a guy just trying to win over the girl of his dreams while dealing with a grumpy father who is not on board with the romance.

What really works here is the funny timing and the way the plot keeps you guessing. You will love the chemistry between the leads, though the pacing feels a bit slow in the middle. Since it is a silent film, you have to pay attention to the facial expressions, but it is still a great watch. It is a perfect pick if you enjoy old-school stories about love and mishaps.
endingExplained: Everything wraps up when Jode finally manages to prove his worth to Peg's father. After a series of funny misunderstandings and some tension on the ranch, the grumpy dad finally sees that Jode truly loves his daughter. The tension breaks, and the father gives them his blessing. Jode and Peg end up together in a happy ending, showing that true love can win over even the toughest boss in the west.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old silent movies and cute romance stories.
